# slf4j-ktx (Kotlin 1.9.25)

> Kotlin 1.9.25 compiler plugin. Annotate a class with `@io.github.harryjhin.slf4j.ktx.Slf4j` and the plugin synthesizes its `Companion` with an internal `log: Logger` plus `trace`/`debug`/`info`/`warn`/`error × 2`. User class body untouched. Lazy: `if (log.isXxxEnabled) log.xxx(message())`. 1-hop meta-annotation trigger. Spring integration via a separate Gradle plugin. K1 and K2 both registered. Branch `1.9.25-release`; rewrite from the legacy `slf4j-extensions` modules — see CHANGELOG.md.

Documentation: https://github.com/HarryJhin/slf4j-api-extensions

## The Problem

Every class that logs repeats the same Logger declaration and manual `isXxxEnabled` guards:

```kotlin
class OrderService {
    private val log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(OrderService::class.java)

    fun process(order: Order) {
        if (log.isTraceEnabled) log.trace("processing: ${order.id}")
        log.info("order completed")
        log.error("processing failed", exception)
    }
}
```

## The Solution

```kotlin
import io.github.harryjhin.slf4j.ktx.Slf4j

@Slf4j
class OrderService {
    fun process(order: Order) {
        trace { "processing: ${order.id}" }
        info { "order completed" }
        error(exception) { "processing failed" }
    }
}
```

Zero boilerplate. Lambda is not evaluated when the level is disabled.

## Installation

```kotlin
plugins {
    kotlin("jvm") version "1.9.25"
    id("io.github.harryjhin.slf4j-ktx") version "1.9.25"   // plugin ver ≡ Kotlin ver
}

dependencies {
    implementation("io.github.harryjhin:slf4j-ktx-core:0.1.0")
    runtimeOnly("org.slf4j:slf4j-simple:2.0.13")
}
```

Plugin version pairs with the Kotlin version. Runtime dependency is explicit (kotlinx-serialization / KSP convention). `slf4j-ktx-core` has an independent cadence (`coreVersion`, starts `0.1.0`) from the compiler-plugin/Kotlin pair.

## Gradle DSL

```kotlin
slf4jKtx {
    annotation("com.example.LoggedDomain")   // additional trigger FQN (multi-valued)
}
```

Single option. `@Slf4j` is always a trigger; `annotation("…")` adds more. No `propertyName`, no `allClasses`, no `packages(…)` — removed in the rewrite.

## Spring Integration

```kotlin
plugins {
    id("io.github.harryjhin.slf4j-ktx.spring") version "1.9.25"
}
```

Auto-applies the main plugin and pushes six Spring stereotype FQNs as triggers:

- `org.springframework.stereotype.Component`
- `org.springframework.stereotype.Controller`
- `org.springframework.stereotype.Service`
- `org.springframework.stereotype.Repository`
- `org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController`
- `org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.ControllerAdvice`

Custom `slf4jKtx { annotation("…") }` entries combine with the Spring FQNs.

## What The Compiler Generates

Source:

```kotlin
@Slf4j
class OrderService {
    fun process() {
        trace { "start" }
        info { "done" }
        error(exception) { "failed" }
    }
}
```

Bytecode-equivalent:

```kotlin
class OrderService {
    fun process() {
        Companion.trace { "start" }     // resolved unqualified by Kotlin scope rules
        Companion.info { "done" }
        Companion.error(exception) { "failed" }
    }

    companion object {
        internal val log: Logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger("com.example.OrderService")

        internal fun trace(message: () -> String) {
            if (log.isTraceEnabled) log.trace(message())
        }
        internal fun trace(throwable: Throwable, message: () -> String) {
            if (log.isTraceEnabled) log.trace(message(), throwable)
        }
        // debug, info, warn, error × 2 — same pattern (10 level functions total)
    }
}
```

User class body is never rewritten. If no Companion exists, the plugin creates one; if one exists, members are added alongside user declarations.

For `@Slf4j object Foo`, members are injected onto the object itself (no Companion; the object is already the singleton).

## Trigger Surface

1. `@io.github.harryjhin.slf4j.ktx.Slf4j` on a class or object (primary).
2. Any FQN registered via `slf4jKtx { annotation("…") }`.
3. Any of the six Spring stereotypes (only when `id("io.github.harryjhin.slf4j-ktx.spring")` is applied).
4. **1-hop meta-annotation** — a user annotation that itself carries one of the above:
   ```kotlin
   @Slf4j
   annotation class LoggedStereotype

   @LoggedStereotype
   class OrderService { fun process() { info { "…" } } }
   ```

Meta-annotation is flat (1 hop). `@Slf4j` → `@LoggedStereotype` → `OrderService` triggers; `@Slf4j` → `@A` → `@B` → `OrderService` does not.

## Skip Conditions

| Kind | Triggered? |
|---|---|
| `class`, `data class`, `enum class`, `sealed class`, `abstract class` | Yes, with a Companion |
| `object` | Yes, members on the object |
| `interface` | No |
| `annotation class` | No (but `@Slf4j` on an annotation class works as a meta-trigger on *classes* that use it) |
| local / anonymous classes | No |

Collision policy (silent skip, matching kotlinx-serialization): if the user has declared a callable with the same name on the generation site (`log`, `trace`, etc.), the plugin emits nothing for that name. No warning, no diagnostic.

## Where Members Are Visible

Companion members are accessible **unqualified from the enclosing class body**. Everywhere else, they are not in scope.

| Context | `info { "…" }` unqualified? |
|---|---|
| Member function / initializer of the annotated class | Yes |
| Local function inside such a member | Yes |
| Nested class inside the annotated class | **No** (nested class needs its own `@Slf4j`) |
| Subclass body (parent is `@Slf4j`, child is not) | **No** (Companion members are not inherited) |
| Top-level function or helper file | **No** |

The rule: each declaration that needs logging gets its own `@Slf4j`. Matches Lombok `@Slf4j` semantics.

## `log` Visibility

The injected `log` property is `internal`. From inside the same module you can reach SLF4J APIs that the lazy-lambda surface doesn't cover (parameterized messages, conditional branches):

```kotlin
@Slf4j
class OrderService {
    fun process() {
        info { "msg" }                     // primary API
        log.info("literal {}", value)      // same module — use the Logger directly
        if (log.isDebugEnabled) expensiveDump()
    }
}
```

Consumers in other modules cannot reach `log`; annotate each class that needs logging with `@Slf4j` — Lombok/kotlinx-serialization convention.

## `kotlin.error()` Disambiguation

```kotlin
error("msg")    // → kotlin.error(Any) → throws IllegalStateException
error { "msg" } // → Companion.error(() -> String) → logs at ERROR level
```

Different call syntax — no resolution ambiguity.

## Runtime Module API (`slf4j-ktx-core`)

### `@Slf4j` annotation

```kotlin
package io.github.harryjhin.slf4j.ktx

@Target(AnnotationTarget.CLASS)
@Retention(AnnotationRetention.BINARY)
annotation class Slf4j
```

### Marker Extensions (10 functions)

Marker-qualified overloads stay in the runtime — they're not Companion members (different call shape).

```kotlin
// MarkerExtensions.kt — invoked as log.info(marker) { "…" }
inline fun Logger.trace(marker: Marker, message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.trace(marker: Marker, throwable: Throwable, message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.debug(marker: Marker, message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.debug(marker: Marker, throwable: Throwable, message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.info(marker: Marker, message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.info(marker: Marker, throwable: Throwable, message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.warn(marker: Marker, message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.warn(marker: Marker, throwable: Throwable, message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.error(marker: Marker, message: () -> String)
inline fun Logger.error(marker: Marker, throwable: Throwable, message: () -> String)
```

Same lazy pattern — `if (isXxxEnabled(marker)) xxx(marker, message())`.

### MDC Utilities

```kotlin
// MdcExtensions.kt
inline fun <R> withMDC(vararg entries: Pair<String, String?>, block: () -> R): R
```

Sets MDC entries for the duration of `block`, restores previous values on exit (exception-safe).

```kotlin
withMDC("requestId" to "abc-123", "userId" to "user-1") {
    info { "processing request" }
}
```

Passing `null` as a value removes the entry temporarily.

## Modules (published)

| Artifact | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `io.github.harryjhin:slf4j-ktx-core` | `@Slf4j` annotation + Marker/MDC inline extensions. Independent `coreVersion`. |
| `io.github.harryjhin:slf4j-ktx-compiler-plugin-embeddable` | Compiler plugin fat JAR. Resolved automatically by the Gradle plugin. |
| `io.github.harryjhin:slf4j-ktx-gradle-plugin` | Main Gradle plugin (`slf4jKtx { }` DSL). |
| `io.github.harryjhin:slf4j-ktx-spring-gradle-plugin` | Spring integration (auto-apply main + Spring stereotype FQNs). |

Internal compiler modules (`slf4j-ktx.common`, `.k1`, `.k2`, `.backend`, `.cli`) are not published.

## Versioning

| Axis | Rule |
|---|---|
| Plugin version | ≡ Kotlin version (e.g. `1.9.25`). |
| `slf4j-ktx-core` | Independent cadence; starts at `0.1.0`. Versioned semantically. |
| `Require-Kotlin-Version` | Stamped in `slf4j-ktx-core`'s `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF`. The plugin's `VersionReader` reads this + `Implementation-Version` and emits `CORE_MISSING` / `CORE_TOO_OLD` / `COMPILER_TOO_OLD` diagnostics when the user's classpath is incompatible with the plugin build. |

## Compatibility

| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Kotlin | 1.9.25 (this branch) |
| Plugin version | = Kotlin version |
| `slf4j-ktx-core` | 0.1.0+ (independent cadence) |
| Java | 8+ runtime target, 17+ to build the project |
| SLF4J | 1.7.36+ (compatible with 2.0) |
| Gradle | 8.0+ |
